report_meta.supply_chain_link: onsemi is the US POWER-SEMICONDUCTOR node in this project's power sub-chain — and it sits at a DIFFERENT layer than the Korean transformer/switchgear makers (Sanil, HD Hyundai Electric, LS Electric). Those companies make the 'iron' (transformers, switchgear) at the grid/substation level; onsemi makes the SILICON — the power chips (silicon carbide, gallium nitride, IGBTs, MOSFETs, power-management ICs) that convert and deliver electricity efficiently INSIDE the AI data-center power tree and inside EVs. Its AI relevance is direct and accelerating: management calls onsemi 'the only broad-based U.S. power semiconductor supplier' for the AI data-center power tree, spanning 'grid to processor' — high-voltage conversion, intermediate bus converters, intelligent power stages, point-of-load/VCORE, and next-gen 800V DC architectures — engaging every major hyperscaler and XPU vendor via power-supply partners (e.g. FlexPower, 30+ programs). The move to 800V/HVDC racks lifts onsemi content from ~$9,500 to ~$115,000 per rack (~10x+). It also supplies EV power (SiC/IGBT traction inverters; ~55% SiC share of new EV models at the 2026 Beijing show) and energy storage (the 'AI halo'). In the graph it sits alongside Vertiv, Eaton, Monolithic Power, Navitas, Power Integrations, Vicor, Infineon, STM and TI (transcripts/power/), and competes mainly with Infineon and STMicroelectronics. Litmus test: does its stock directly benefit from AI data centers being built? YES — power semiconductors are essential to AI server power delivery, and content per rack is exploding with the 800V transition.

beginner_glossary.onsemi (ON Semiconductor): A US semiconductor company that makes POWER chips and image SENSORS. Spun off from Motorola in 1999, it specializes in chips that manage and convert electricity efficiently — used in electric vehicles, factories/energy systems, and increasingly AI data centers. It is a recovery-and-AI-power story after a deep auto/industrial downturn in 2024–2025.
beginner_glossary.Power semiconductor: A chip that switches or converts electrical power (rather than processing data). Power chips control how electricity flows — turning high voltage into the precise low voltage a processor needs, with as little energy lost as heat as possible. onsemi is one of the world's leading power-chip makers.
beginner_glossary.Silicon carbide (SiC / EliteSiC): A next-generation chip material that handles high voltage and heat far better than ordinary silicon — ideal for EV powertrains and high-power data-center conversion. onsemi's brand is 'EliteSiC'; it is a SiC market leader (e.g. ~55% share of new EV models shown at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show).
beginner_glossary.Gallium nitride (GaN): Another advanced chip material, best for high-frequency, high-efficiency power conversion (e.g. inside data-center power supplies and chargers). onsemi's GaN design pipeline exceeds $1.5B, with revenue starting in 2027.
beginner_glossary.IGBT / MOSFET: Two common types of power-switching transistor. IGBTs suit cost-optimized high-power uses (e.g. EV traction inverters); MOSFETs (incl. SiC MOSFETs) suit higher-frequency switching. onsemi makes both.
beginner_glossary.Treo platform: onsemi's flexible analog/mixed-signal chip platform on which it builds many application-specific products. It carries high gross margins (60–70%) and is ramping fast (revenue +2.5x in Q1 2026); targeted to reach ~$1B of revenue by 2030.
beginner_glossary.Power tree (grid-to-processor): The chain of power conversions from the wall/grid down to the chip: high-voltage conversion → intermediate bus converters (IBC) → intelligent power stages (SPS) → point-of-load/VCORE right at the GPU/CPU. onsemi sells chips at EVERY step — its 'grid to processor' pitch.
beginner_glossary.VCORE / point-of-load: The final, lowest-voltage power delivered right next to the processor core. A large, growing opportunity (esp. for new server CPUs); onsemi entered it via its Aurasemi acquisition (multiphase controllers/regulators).
beginner_glossary.800V DC / HVDC data center: Next-generation data-center power architecture that distributes electricity at much higher voltage (800 volts DC) to cut losses as AI racks get huge. This shift roughly 10x's onsemi's chip content per rack (from ~$9,500 to ~$115,000).
beginner_glossary.Hyperscaler / XPU: Hyperscalers are the giant clouds (the AI data-center buyers). 'XPU' = any AI accelerator (GPU/CPU/custom ASIC). onsemi supplies power chips for all of them, often through power-supply vendors (e.g. FlexPower).
beginner_glossary.Energy storage (ESS) / AI halo: Battery energy-storage systems. As AI raises power demand and costs, energy storage and microgrids boom — the 'AI halo effect.' onsemi's ESS business is growing >40% with ~60% share (via SiC hybrid modules).
beginner_glossary.PSG / AMG / ISG: onsemi's three reporting groups: PSG = Power Solutions Group (power chips — the largest, ~$737M/qtr); AMG = Analog & Mixed-Signal Group (~$540M); ISG = Intelligent Sensing Group (image sensors/ToF, ~$256M).
beginner_glossary.FabRight: onsemi's manufacturing-optimization program — closing/divesting less-efficient fabs and improving utilization to structurally raise gross margin. A core part of the margin-expansion thesis.
beginner_glossary.GAAP vs non-GAAP: GAAP is official accounting (includes everything, e.g. big restructuring/impairment charges). Non-GAAP strips those out. CRITICAL for onsemi: its GAAP earnings are badly distorted by restructuring/impairments (Q1 2026 had a $329M restructuring charge → a GAAP loss), so its trailing GAAP P/E (~83x) is misleading. Use non-GAAP (Q1 2026 EPS $0.64) to judge the business.
beginner_glossary.Gross margin: Percent of revenue left after the direct cost of making the chips. onsemi's non-GAAP gross margin was 38.5% in Q1 2026 and rising — management targets the 50s% longer term via FabRight, higher utilization, and a richer mix (SiC/GaN/Treo at 60–70%).
beginner_glossary.Utilization: How fully the factories run. onsemi was at 77% in Q1 2026; each point adds ~25–30 bps of gross margin. Reaching the low-90s would need ~25–30% more revenue — i.e. lots of operating leverage as the cycle recovers.
beginner_glossary.Cyclical / inflection: Chip demand for autos and industry runs in boom/bust cycles. After ~7 down quarters, onsemi says Q1 2026 is the 'inflection point' — the cycle has bottomed and is recovering, with AI data center adding structural growth on top.
beginner_glossary.Free cash flow (FCF): Cash left after running the business and capex. onsemi generated $1.4B in FY2025 (24% margin) even in a down year — and returns ~100% of it to shareholders via buybacks (no dividend).
beginner_glossary.P/E ratio (price-to-earnings): Share price ÷ yearly earnings per share. onsemi's trailing GAAP P/E (~83x) is inflated by depressed/restructuring-hit earnings; its forward P/E on non-GAAP estimates is ~35x — high, but it prices a cyclical recovery plus AI-power growth.

company_snapshot.what_it_is: onsemi is a US maker of power semiconductors and image sensors. It supplies the chips that convert and deliver electricity efficiently — for electric vehicles, industrial/energy systems, and (fast-growing) AI data centers — plus sensing chips for automotive and robotics. After a deep 2024–2025 auto/industrial downcycle (revenue fell 15% in 2025), it says Q1 2026 marks an inflection: the cycle is recovering while AI data-center power and a leaner, higher-margin model drive structural growth. As of June 2026 it carries a ~$46B market cap.
company_snapshot.ceo: Hassane El-Khoury (President & CEO); Thad Trent (EVP & CFO)
company_snapshot.founded: 1999 (spun off from Motorola's Semiconductor Components Group); listed on NASDAQ
company_snapshot.where_it_sits_in_the_chain: The power-SEMICONDUCTOR layer of this project's power sub-chain — the silicon inside the power tree, distinct from the grid-level transformer/switchgear makers. It SELLS power chips (SiC, GaN, IGBT, MOSFET, power-management, VCORE) and sensors to AI data centers (via power-supply vendors and XPU/hyperscaler engagements), automotive OEMs (EV powertrain/ADAS), and industrial/energy-storage customers. It BUYS wafers/materials and runs its own fabs (with SiC substrate vertically integrated). It competes mainly with Infineon and STMicroelectronics.
company_snapshot.manufacturing_note: onsemi runs its own fabs but has been restructuring ('FabRight' — divesting/closing less-efficient fabs, raising utilization) to lift margins; capex is lean (~mid-single-digit % of revenue). Utilization was 77% in Q1 2026 with ~25–30% revenue headroom before needing new capacity (e.g. Treo ramps from East Fishkill). It has vertically integrated SiC (substrate via the former GTAT) and made bolt-on acquisitions (Aurasemi for VCORE, a SiC JFET line, vertical GaN from NextGen).
products: Power Solutions (PSG): SiC (EliteSiC), GaN, IGBTs, MOSFETs, power modules, intelligent power stages — for EVs, data centers, energy storage
Analog & Mixed-Signal (AMG): the Treo platform, power-management, VCORE/multiphase controllers, connectivity (10BASE-T1S Ethernet for zonal autos)
Intelligent Sensing (ISG): image sensors, time-of-flight (ToF), SWIR — for automotive ADAS, industrial autonomy and robotics
AI data-center power: full 'power tree' from high-voltage/800V DC conversion to point-of-load VCORE
end_markets: Industrial (energy storage/ESS, microgrid, factory automation, medical)

business_model.summary: onsemi designs and manufactures power and sensing semiconductors and sells them into three end markets — automotive, industrial, and (increasingly) AI data centers. Its strategy under CEO Hassane El-Khoury has been to RESTRUCTURE into a leaner, higher-margin, power-and-sensing-focused company: divesting fabs, exiting ~$300M/year of low-margin 'non-core' business, and concentrating R&D/capital on high-value transitions (SiC, GaN, the Treo platform, AI data-center power). The result is a model built for operating leverage — as the auto/industrial cycle recovers and AI data center ramps, incremental revenue is meant to fall through to much higher margins and free cash flow, ~100% of which is returned via buybacks.
how_they_make_money: Power Solutions Group (PSG, the engine): SiC/GaN/IGBT/MOSFET power chips and modules. $737M in Q1 2026 (+14% YoY) — the fastest-growing group, carrying EV power and AI data-center power.
Analog & Mixed-Signal (AMG): Treo platform, power management, VCORE, connectivity. $540M in Q1 2026 (−5% YoY) — the margin-rich Treo (60–70%) is ramping here.
Intelligent Sensing (ISG): image sensors and ToF for automotive, industrial autonomy and robotics. $256M in Q1 2026.
By end market (Q1 2026): Automotive $797M, Industrial $417M, 'Other' $299M (includes AI data center).
AI data center (within PSG/Other): grew >30% QoQ / doubled YoY; ~$250M in 2025 expected to DOUBLE to ~$500M in 2026. Capital returns: ~100% of FCF via buybacks (no dividend).
competitive_moat_analyst_view: Breadth of power technologies: 'the only broad-based U.S. power semiconductor supplier' for the AI data-center power tree (grid to processor) — SiC, GaN, IGBT, MOSFET, power-management, VCORE in one portfolio. [Q1 2026 call] [analyst interpretation]
SiC leadership + vertical integration: EliteSiC with in-house substrate; ~55% SiC share of new EV models at the 2026 Beijing show; preferred for 900V Chinese EV platforms (Geely, NIO). [Q1 2026 call]
Treo platform: a versatile analog/mixed-signal platform at 60–70% gross margin, ramping fast and targeted to ~$1B by 2030 — a structural margin and growth driver. [Q1 2026 call]
Leaner cost structure (FabRight): restructuring and fab divestitures designed to lift gross margin toward the 50s% with strong operating leverage as volumes recover. [Q1 2026 call]
CAVEAT: power semis are competitive and cyclical — Infineon (the larger leader) and STMicroelectronics are formidable, so the 'moat' is real but contested. [analyst interpretation]

revenue_streams.analyst_view: Two engines are turning at once. The CYCLICAL one: automotive (~53% of revenue) just posted its first YoY growth after seven down quarters, and industrial is stabilizing — onsemi says it is now 'shipping to natural demand,' i.e. the inventory correction is over. The STRUCTURAL one: AI data center (small today, ~$500M/yr, but doubling) plus the high-margin Treo platform and SiC/GaN. The bull case is operating leverage as both turn up; the watch-item is that AI data center is still only ~8% of revenue, so the bulk of the story still rides the auto/industrial recovery actually playing out.

industry_trends.why_it_matters: AI servers need vastly more, denser, more efficient power conversion. As the only broad-based US power-semi supplier across the full power tree, onsemi gains content at every step — and the 800V/HVDC shift ~10x's its content per rack.
industry_trends.evidence: AI data-center revenue +30% QoQ / 2x YoY, guided to double in 2026; rack content ~$9,500 (120kW) → ~$115,000 (800V); 30+ FlexPower programs across all hyperscalers. [Q1 2026 call, 2026-05-04]

competitors.landscape_summary: onsemi competes in power and sensing semiconductors. Its principal rival is Infineon — the global power-semiconductor leader (larger, broad SiC/IGBT/power-management) — followed by STMicroelectronics (also strong in SiC and automotive). In data-center point-of-load/VCORE and power-management it meets Monolithic Power, Texas Instruments, Analog Devices, Navitas, Power Integrations and Vicor; in SiC specifically, Wolfspeed and STM; in microcontrollers/analog adjacencies, Renesas and Microchip. onsemi's pitch is breadth (the full power tree from one US supplier) plus SiC leadership and the high-margin Treo platform; the competitive risk is that larger, well-capitalized rivals (especially Infineon) press on price and scale, and that data-center power attracts intense competition.

competitors.differentiation_analyst_view: onsemi differentiates on breadth (a US one-stop power-tree supplier), SiC leadership with vertical integration, and the high-margin Treo platform. The competitive risk is scale: Infineon is larger and equally focused on data-center/EV power, and the data-center point-of-load market (Monolithic Power's stronghold) is crowded. onsemi's edge is real but must be defended against bigger balance sheets — and a chunk of the thesis (margin expansion) depends on internal execution (FabRight) as much as on winning share.

financial_performance.analyst_view: The financial story is an INFLECTION off a trough. FY2025 was weak (revenue −15%, GAAP EPS depressed), but Q1 2026 shows the turn: revenue +5% YoY, non-GAAP gross margin up a third straight quarter to 38.5%, automotive growing again, AI data center doubling, and a lean cost base built for operating leverage. Two things to hold: (1) judge profitability on NON-GAAP — GAAP is distorted by restructuring (a $329M charge caused a GAAP loss in Q1); and (2) the margin-expansion-to-the-50s% thesis is partly self-help (FabRight/mix/utilization) that must execute. Free cash flow is strong (24% margin even in a down year) and fully returned via buybacks.

valuation.analyst_view: onsemi is a cyclical-recovery-plus-AI-power re-rating. The quality is improving (leaner model, rising gross margin, strong FCF), and the AI data-center content story (grid-to-processor, 800V, ~10x rack content) is genuinely attractive. But the valuation already reflects a lot of optimism: the stock has ~2.5x'd off its low, sits near its 52-week high, trades slightly ABOVE the ~$105 consensus target, and carries ~35x forward non-GAAP earnings — for a business still ~80% dependent on auto/industrial cycles that are only just turning. The honest read: real inflection and real AI optionality, but priced for the recovery and margin expansion to deliver, with the small (~8%) AI data-center base meaning the near-term result still hinges on the auto/industrial cycle.

risks.why_it_matters: Most revenue still rides auto/industrial chip cycles that are only just turning; a stalled recovery would hit the bulk of the business and the operating-leverage thesis.
The stock has ~2.5x'd off its low, trades near its 52-week high and ABOVE the ~$105 consensus target at ~35x forward non-GAAP — little cushion if results disappoint.

risks.risk: AI data center still small (~8% of revenue)
risks.why_it_matters: The exciting AI-power story (~$500M in 2026) is real but not yet big enough to carry the company; the near-term result depends on the cyclical recovery.
Much of the thesis is self-help (utilization, fab divestitures, mix to 50s% gross margin) that must execute on schedule to justify the multiple.
Larger, well-capitalized rivals compete hard in SiC/EV power and crowded data-center point-of-load — pressuring share and pricing.

risks.risk: EV / SiC demand and China dependence
risks.why_it_matters: A chunk of SiC growth leans on Chinese EV platforms; an EV-demand slowdown or China policy/geopolitics could hit SiC volumes.
Recurring restructuring/impairment charges depress GAAP results (a $329M charge caused a GAAP loss in Q1 2026), making headline earnings noisy and the trailing P/E misleading.
AI data-center content is largely won through a few power-supply vendors and hyperscaler-defined architectures, concentrating that growth channel.
201 days of inventory (incl. 75 strategic) is high; depletion is planned over ~2 years, but a demand wobble could pressure margins/cash.
Input costs are already in the P&L while offsetting price increases lag into H2 2026 — a near-term margin timing risk.

scenarios.disclaimer: Illustrative scenarios to frame the range of outcomes — NOT predictions, targets, or advice.

bull_case.thesis: The auto/industrial cycle recovers strongly, AI data center keeps doubling, SiC/GaN/Treo drive a rich mix, and FabRight lifts gross margin toward the 50s% — delivering powerful operating leverage on a lean cost base.
key_drivers: Auto and industrial re-accelerate (second half outgrows first half), lifting utilization and margins.
AI data center compounds (800V content ~10x; VCORE/GaN add legs) well beyond the ~$500M 2026 base.
Treo scales toward $1B (2030) at 60–70% margin; SiC share gains continue (China 900V).
Gross margin marches toward the 50s%; non-GAAP EPS rises fast, deflating the forward multiple.
~100% of growing FCF returned via buybacks.
bull_case.what_to_watch: Auto/industrial order trends; AI DC growth; gross-margin step-ups; Treo/SiC/GaN ramps; utilization toward 90%.

base_case.thesis: A real but measured recovery: revenue grows mid-to-high single digits in 2026, margins expand gradually, and AI data center adds a growing but still-minor contribution.
key_drivers: Revenue ~$6.5B in 2026 (+8%); gross margin grinds higher (38.5% → low-40s%).
Auto/industrial recover but not sharply; AI data center doubles to ~$500M.
Non-GAAP EPS rises ~30% (~$3.09); the stock tracks earnings rather than further multiple expansion.
FabRight delivers incremental (not step-change) margin gains; buybacks continue.
Competition keeps pricing disciplined but contained.
base_case.what_to_watch: Revenue trajectory vs the ~$6.47B estimate; gross-margin cadence; non-core-exit completion; AI DC mix.

bear_case.thesis: The auto/industrial recovery stalls, margin expansion underdelivers, competition intensifies, and a stock that ~2.5x'd and trades above consensus de-rates from ~35x forward.
key_drivers: Auto/industrial demand softens again (EV slowdown, macro) — the ~80% base disappoints.
AI data center stays too small to offset; growth decelerates as competition (Infineon/MPS) bites.
Gross-margin gains stall (utilization, pricing-lag, mix) below the 50s% target.
Restructuring/impairments persist, keeping GAAP noisy and sentiment cautious.
The forward multiple compresses toward sales-based levels — meaningful downside from the highs.
bear_case.what_to_watch: Any auto/industrial order rollover; gross-margin stall; share/pricing pressure; AI DC growth slowing; weak guidance.

final_research_summary.one_paragraph: onsemi (ON) is a US power-and-sensing semiconductor maker positioned at a different layer of this project's power chain than the Korean transformer/switchgear names: it makes the SILICON — silicon carbide, gallium nitride, IGBTs, MOSFETs, power-management ICs and image sensors — that converts and delivers electricity inside AI data centers and EVs. After a deep 2024–2025 downcycle (FY2025 revenue $6.0B, −15%; GAAP EPS depressed to $0.29 by restructuring), management says Q1 2026 (reported 2026-05-04) marks the inflection: revenue rose +5% YoY to $1.51B with non-GAAP EPS of $0.64, non-GAAP gross margin expanded for a third straight quarter to 38.5%, automotive grew year-over-year for the first time in seven quarters, and AI data-center revenue grew >30% sequentially and doubled YoY (guided to double again in 2026, ~$250M → ~$500M). The structural story is attractive — onsemi calls itself 'the only broad-based U.S. power semiconductor supplier' for the full AI data-center power tree (grid-to-processor), where the 800V/HVDC shift lifts its content per rack roughly 10x (from ~$9,500 to ~$115,000) — layered on SiC EV leadership (~55% share of 2026 Beijing-show models, 900V China platforms), a high-margin Treo platform (60–70% gross margin, targeted $1B by 2030), GaN (revenue from 2027) and a FabRight margin-expansion plan toward the 50s%. Two analytical must-knows: judge profitability on NON-GAAP (a $329M restructuring charge produced a GAAP loss in Q1 2026, so the ~83x trailing GAAP P/E is meaningless), and free cash flow is strong (24% margin even in a down year) and ~100% returned via buybacks (no dividend). On valuation, the stock (~$116.79; ~$46B market cap; ~35x FY2026 forward non-GAAP EPS of ~$3.09; ~7.6x sales) has already ~2.5x'd off its 52-week low ($44.56), trades near its high ($134.92) and ABOVE the ~$105.45 analyst consensus target — i.e. the average analyst sees modest downside while bulls (high target $150) see more. The honest read: a genuine cyclical inflection plus credible AI-power optionality and self-help margin expansion, but priced for it — with AI data center still only ~8% of revenue, the near-term result hinges on the auto/industrial recovery actually delivering, against a forward multiple that leaves little cushion.
